single.title: One considered copy
single.description: Start with one 4-bit encoding, then make it yours.
single.note: A storage-oriented starting point, not a benchmark or a hardware-fit guarantee.

compare.title: A comparison pair
compare.description: Keep a compact encoding and an 8-bit counterpart.
compare.note: Compare these published encodings on your own tasks. More bytes alone do not prove better answers.

whole.title: The whole publication
whole.description: Every published file, every variant, every companion.
whole.note: For collecting this repository as published. This includes every file at the inspected revision.

float.label: Floating-point encoding
float.meaning: A wide numerical representation. BF16 and F16 use 16 bits per stored weight; F32 uses 32.
float.collect: Keep this when this particular published encoding matters, or when a compatible toolchain needs it. A wider encoding does not establish an original training checkpoint.

wide.label: Roomier quantization
wide.meaning: A 6- or 8-bit family leaves more room to represent weights than a lower-bit encoding. Actual files also contain scales and metadata.
wide.collect: A useful counterpart when comparing published quantizations. Quality and speed still depend on the model, recipe, runtime, and hardware.

middle.label: Middle-ground footprint
middle.meaning: A 4- or 5-bit family trades numerical detail for a smaller stored representation. Mixed-precision recipes can use wider types for some tensors.
middle.collect: A place to start exploring a compact copy, provided your runtime supports it. Evaluate your own tasks; the label is not a quality score.

compact.label: Small-footprint encoding
compact.meaning: A 1-, 2-, or 3-bit family pushes storage lower. These are encoding families, not literal file-size formulas or performance rankings.
compact.collect: Collect for constrained storage, experimentation, or the history of an aggressive quantization recipe. Check model-specific evaluations before relying on it.

unknown.label: Published encoding
unknown.meaning: The filename does not identify an encoding family darsay understands. Its files and measured size still matter.
unknown.collect: Inspect the publisher's model card and runtime requirements. Unknown terminology is not a reason to discard a publication.

recovery.label: Exact recovery unverified
recovery.description: An inventory and a precision label cannot tell us how hard these exact bytes are to recreate. That needs pinned source weights, tools, settings, any calibration inputs, and matching output hashes.
recovery.note: A related base model or a working conversion is not a verified reconstruction. No recreation-cost estimate is claimed.

companions: Projectors are companions, not smaller copies of the language model. Multimodal use may need a matching projector. Choose one according to the publisher and runtime; darsay does not infer compatibility from precision.
companion_collect: Keep the companion needed by the multimodal workflow you intend to preserve, or collect its published alternatives. Consult the publisher and runtime for compatibility; companions are not interchangeable just because their precision labels match.
scope: Unselected artifacts are outside this collection, not proven disposable. Adding to a board downloads no model bytes.
sizing: Sizes include every shard. Selection totals count shared support files once. Disk size is not a RAM or VRAM requirement.
